plan: Fill the graveyard, sacrifice creatures for value, and bring the best of them back with Meren every end step.

review.text:
HOW IT WINS. Turns 1-3 are setup, and the deck has plenty of it: Stitcher's Supplier, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Gravecrawler and Spore Frog at one mana, with Grisly Salvage, Mulch, Stinkweed Imp's dredge 5 and Golgari Grave-Troll's dredge 6 to put creature cards where you want them. Nothing here is trying to affect the board yet - it is filling the yard and setting up a sacrifice outlet.

Turns 4-6 are where Meren lands and the deck turns on. Each creature that dies gives an experience counter, and at every end step she returns a creature card whose mana value is at most your experience count to the battlefield - otherwise to your hand. Paired with Carrion Feeder, Nantuko Husk, Viscera Seer, Ghoulcaller Gisa or Phyrexian Tower, the small value creatures become a loop: Fleshbag Marauder, Plaguecrafter, Ravenous Chupacabra, Shriekmaw, Acidic Slime and Reclamation Sage all have enter-the-battlefield effects you can buy again and again. Grave Pact and Dictate of Erebos turn each of those sacrifices into an opponent sacrificing too. The one-shot reanimation - Victimize, Animate Dead, Necromancy, Dread Return - cashes in early mill for something large ahead of schedule.

Turns 7 and on, the top end arrives: Living Death as a one-sided reset when your graveyard is full and theirs is not, Massacre Wurm wiping small boards and draining, Butcher of Malakir making every death a board-wide sacrifice, Woodfall Primus with persist against a key permanent, Moldgraf Monstrosity returning two creatures at random when it dies.

What actually ends the game is the drain: Blood Artist and Zulaport Cutthroat convert a sacrifice loop into life loss across the table. That is only two cards, and they are the only cards that kill without combat. Otherwise you are attacking with Splinterfright and Golgari Grave-Troll, both of which grow with creature cards in the graveyard, or grinding opponents to nothing with Grave Pact effects until your creatures get through. It is a real plan, but it is slow, and it depends on finding one of two drain pieces.

CURVE AGAINST LANDS AND RAMP. Average mana value is 3.03, and the curve is bunched: 18 cards at two and 22 at three, then only 4 at four and 11 cards at five or more. Lands are at 37 against a target of 38. Ramp is at 5 against a target of 10 - the largest gap in the deck. With 5 ramp pieces (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Golgari Signet, Cultivate, Sakura-Tribe Elder) Meren mostly arrives on turn four off land drops alone, which is acceptable, but Butcher of Malakir at 7, Moldgraf Monstrosity at 7 and Woodfall Primus at 8 are cards you will rarely cast. That is half forgiven by the deck's nature - you would rather reanimate them than pay for them - but five more ramp pieces would mean Meren on turn three and a second spell alongside her, which is the difference between this deck's engine starting on time and starting late.

Colours are clean: 58 black pips against 24 sources, 27 green pips against 21 sources. The black-heavy requirement is matched by the black-heavier land base, and the heaviest costs - Grave Pact at {1}{B}{B}{B}, Massacre Wurm at {3}{B}{B}{B} - are supported.

WHEN THE COMMANDER IS ANSWERED. Better than most commander-engine decks. Meren is the only repeatable recursion, so losing her slows you down, but the deck keeps recursion that does not need her: Animate Dead, Necromancy, Victimize, Dread Return, Living Death and Moldgraf Monstrosity, plus Bloodghast returning on each landfall, Gravecrawler recastable from the yard with a Zombie out, and the dredge on Stinkweed Imp, Golgari Grave-Troll and Life from the Loam. Card advantage at 11 against a target of 12 is also mostly death-triggered - Grim Haruspex, Midnight Reaper, Harvester of Souls, Fecundity, Deathreap Ritual - so your sacrifice loops keep paying while she is gone. And experience counters do not leave when she does: a recast Meren comes back to the same counter count and immediately returns something big. The weak spot is repeated exile answers, not a single kill spell.

CATEGORIES.
- Ramp, 5 of 10. Discussed above; the real cost is Meren's arrival turn and your ability to cast the top end at all.
- Lands, 37 of 38. One short. Minor on its own, but combined with light ramp the deck is slightly more land-dependent than its land count admits.
- Targeted disruption, 16 of 12. Four over, and the excess is redundancy rather than coverage: Naturalize, Krosan Grip, Reclamation Sage and Acidic Slime all answer artifacts and enchantments, and Doom Blade, Go for the Throat, Infernal Grasp, Murder, Hero's Downfall, Shriekmaw and Ravenous Chupacabra all kill one creature. The creature-bodied ones (Chupacabra, Shriekmaw, Slime, Sage) earn their slots twice because Meren rebuys them; the pure instants do not, and they are the first place to find room for ramp.
- Mass disruption, 5 of 6. One short, and Spore Frog counts here only on a stretch: it prevents all combat damage that would be dealt this turn, which is a fog, not an answer to many of an opponent's things. It is excellent in this deck - Meren returns it every end step for a permanent combat lock - but the category is thinner than 5 suggests. Worth noting Bojuka Bog exiles a player's graveyard when it enters and is not counted here at all.
- Card advantage, 11 of 12. One short, and Viscera Seer counts here on a stretch: sacrifice a creature to scry 1 is selection, it never turns one card into more than one. Fecundity is also symmetric - every player draws on their creatures dying.
- Plan, 40 of 30. Ten over, which is the mirror of the ramp gap. The plan is well served at 41 of 99 cards serving the theme; it just took the mana from somewhere.

LANDS THAT MAKE NO MANA. One: Evolving Wilds, which sacrifices itself to fetch a basic land onto the battlefield tapped. In a deck with 12 Forests and 13 Swamps it always finds something, and sacrificing it is mild graveyard filler, but it is a tapped land on the turn you use it.

Bracket is at 2, which is the target, with no Game Changers, and nothing flagged for singleton, colour identity or legality.

maybeboard.name: Solemn Simulacrum
maybeboard.why: Ramp is at 5 against a target of 10; Doom Blade is the most conditional of the deck's many unconditional kill spells. Solemn Simulacrum ramps on entry, draws on death, and Meren returns it every end step.

maybeboard.name: Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord
maybeboard.why: The review found only two non-combat kills (Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat) and a slow finish. Jarad turns any fat graveyard creature into a table-wide life hit, repeats with Meren, and rebuys himself from the yard. Hero's Downfall is the costliest of six unconditional creature kills.

maybeboard.name: Damnation
maybeboard.why: Mass disruption is at 5 against a target of 6, and Spore Frog counts there only on a stretch. A symmetrical wipe is one-sided in a Meren deck: your board goes to the yard where you want it and she hands it back. Go for the Throat is the one kill spell an artifact creature blanks.
